newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore opposition leaders in contempt of parliament.
newsitem.headline: S'pore opposition leaders in contempt of parliament.

text.p: A Singapore parliamentary committee said on Friday four leaders of the main opposition party had acted in contempt of parliament over incorrect health care spending figures and recommended that they be fined.

The committee of privileges recommended in a report that parliament fine Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) secretary-general Chee Soon Juan S$25,000 (US$17,900) and that three other SDP leaders get fines ranging from S$5,000 to S$13,000.
The maximum punishment for contempt of parliament is a fine of S$50,000 and a jail term.
Chee and the others could also be barred from contesting future elections if the case were passed on to a civil court which then found against them.
But if parliament follows the committee recommendations, that should leave the four free to run in the general election Singapore must hold by April. Chee is widely expected to do so.
He was not available for comment on Friday.

The committee found that Chee, who has the highest profile in the SDP, had fabricated data and falsified documents presented to a Select Committee on health care and subsequently misled the committee when challenged over the figures.
The others were found in contempt in relation to the same committee hearings.

Chee told the committee the figure was a typing mistake and a result of human error. "I deny the allegation that I have presented false documents to the Select Committee with the intent to deceive," he said.

An SDP document submitted to the Select Committee in August had claimed government spending on health care had fallen to only five percent of Singapore's gross domestic product in the 1990s from around 40 percent 20 years earlier.
The figure for the 1990s was incorrect and should have been 25.4 percent, the SDP later admitted.

In its 200-page report, the committee said Chee was "by far the most culpable" of the four as he had "fabricated data and falsified documents with the sole purpose of misleading the Select Committee".
The report also charged Chee with persuading his fellow SDP members "to take positions which they could not have honestly believed to give credence to his contrived explanations".
